summary: This bill amends section 309 of the Clean Air Act to restrict EPA review and written comments to proposed legislation only, by removing all requirements to review or comment on federal construction projects, major agency actions, and proposed regulations from other agencies.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Clean Air Act to reduce EPA review requirements for federal projects and regulations. It has no provisions that increase or decrease government spending levels, appropriations, or budgets.
No provisions relate to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any form of taxation.
The legislation addresses environmental regulatory review and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains nothing related to immigration, border policy, or pathways for legal status.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.

While the bill removes EPA review of certain federal construction projects (which could theoretically include defense-related ones), it does not alter military budgets, defense policy, or spending levels.

The bill explicitly amends Section 309 of the Clean Air Act to eliminate EPA review and comment requirements on proposed federal projects, major agency actions requiring NEPA review, and proposed federal regulations. This directly reduces environmental regulatory oversight and is intended to eliminate duplicative environmental regulations, aligning strongly with limiting environmental regulations.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
The legislation has no bearing on schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions relate to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill makes no changes to fiscal policy, deficits, or debt reduction measures.
No content addresses LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation does not involve foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
No provisions concern voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
The bill has no relation to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No references to labor rights, unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The legislation does not address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
